statement: A call shard whose declared selector exceeds one batch is executed through a bounded deterministic page protocol owned by the existing call batch executor: every page has stable invocation/shard/page identity, advances a monotonic cursor, honors the one absolute deadline and resource budgets, applies backpressure, journals replay safely, and contributes to one complete result without materializing the full shard or silently skipping rows. Verified at HEAD 761dc17c7: shard inputs above BATCH_ROW_BOUND (4096) fail closed with BATCH_BOUND_EXCEEDED and no page identity, cursor, or continuation exists in the batch executor or invoker.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn an independent verifier before audit and handoff and record its stable evidence id.
The call batch executor owns paging; the invoker and reduce coordinator keep their orchestration and completion ownership. No alternate fan-out runtime or bypass of the canonical dispatch path.

Do not implement until the design decisions are a versioned spec under solve/specs/: keyset cursor vs engine cursor, snapshot behavior across pages, component ABI (one run per page plus shard-local combine vs streaming guest session), per-page/per-shard/global partial limits, cancellation and deadline cleanup, retry after ambiguous page execution, movement between pages, and maximum retained coordination state.

Larger-than-one-batch execution uses the explicit page protocol with backpressure, budgets, and deadline behavior; silently raising BATCH_ROW_BOUND or other defaults until the test passes is a failing result.

Removing page identity, cursor persistence, or the memory bound must fail deterministically; the live scenario covers inputs well above 4096 rows per selected shard with no lost or duplicate rows, retry and restart, movement between pages, deadline exhaustion, backpressure, and an independent oracle.
